mssql.label: SQL Server

connect.accepts: An ADO.NET connection string, an mssql:// or JDBC URL, or host,port/database. Azure SQL without a user name signs in with your az login (Entra ID).

limitations: Query Store records aggregate executions and plan history, not an application's request trace or every parameter value. Caller identity and transaction boundaries need application telemetry.

An estimated or stored compilation plan does not measure the rows, timing or waits of the run you are investigating. Runtime-only problems require recorded runtime evidence or an explicitly measured run.

Host CPU and filesystem capacity need their own measurements, such as connected cloud telemetry. Backup recoverability and database corruption are not checked by the statistics scan; they need backup/recovery validation and an appropriate integrity investigation.

postgres.label: PostgreSQL

connect.accepts: A postgres:// or JDBC URL, libpq's key=value pairs, an Npgsql connection string, or host:port/database.

limitations: pg_stat_statements keeps aggregate totals, not per-request traces, historical parameter values or the plan used by each execution. Culprit's scans provide comparisons only over their recorded intervals.
A newly obtained generic plan uses this connection's role, settings and search path; it may differ from the application's custom plan. Actual rows, spills and timing require a measured plan.
Deadlock graphs, statement errors and auto_explain output live in server logs. SQL counters alone cannot reconstruct them; import the relevant logs or correlate application telemetry.

last_actual_plan.message: PostgreSQL doesn't keep the actual plan of past runs
last_actual_plan.hint: auto_explain can write them to the server log, which Culprit can't read over SQL. Open the query in the editor with real values and use Analyze: it runs inside a transaction that is rolled back.

operator_progress.message: PostgreSQL reports a running statement's progress, not each step's
operator_progress.hint: Its plan doesn't change while it runs: ask for the plan once.

yugabyte.label: YugabyteDB

connect.accepts: A YSQL postgres:// or yugabyte:// URL, libpq parameters, or host:port/database.

limitations: YSQL uses DocDB/RocksDB over Raft. PostgreSQL heap pages, buffer-cache ratios, dead tuples, vacuum and XID ages are not storage measurements here.
Local statistics cover the connected YB-TServer. Configured cluster views add other nodes; skipped nodes and independent counter resets prevent complete comparisons.
Captured generic plans use this login's current role and settings. Actual DocDB RPCs and rows scanned require EXPLAIN ANALYZE with DIST.
An index's sharding keys affect distributed reads and write hotspots. Suggested ordered keys use explicit ASC/DESC; review partitioning before deployment.

deadlocks.message: DocDB's distributed deadlock detection is not PostgreSQL's heap lock accounting. A PostgreSQL deadlock counter does not establish this database's distributed deadlocks.
deadlocks.hint: Correlate YSQL errors and the YB-TServer logs for the affected transaction.

last_actual_plan.message: YSQL statement totals do not retain the measured plan of every past execution
last_actual_plan.hint: Analyze a representative statement to capture its actual DocDB work.

operator_progress.message: YSQL does not expose live row counters for every plan operator
operator_progress.hint: Use a measured plan and native statement/operation progress.

mysql.label: MySQL

connect.accepts: A mysql://, mariadb:// or JDBC URL, a .NET connection string (Server=…;Uid=…), or host:port/database.

limitations: Statement digests keep aggregate totals, not an application's request trace, transaction boundaries or the plan of every historical execution. Culprit compares only intervals its scans or the slow log record.
InnoDB status keeps only the latest deadlock. A complete incident history requires the error log; an empty or old latest report does not prove that no other deadlocks happened.
MySQL and MariaDB differ in plan details, instrumentation and syntax. Runtime measurements, metadata-lock visibility and replication diagnostics depend on the product, version and permissions.

last_actual_plan.message: MySQL and MariaDB don't keep the actual plan of past runs
last_actual_plan.hint: Measure it instead: Analyze runs the statement's recorded text once inside a read-only transaction.

operator_progress.message: MySQL reports a running statement's progress, not each step's
operator_progress.hint: Its plan doesn't change while it runs: ask for the plan once.

sqlite.label: SQLite

connect.accepts: The database file. Culprit opens it read-only and needs nothing from your app.

limitations: SQLite file inspection cannot see the application's connections, transaction owners, foreign_keys, busy_timeout or synchronous settings. Configure and inspect those on the application's own connections.

Plans are obtained with Culprit's SQLite library, which may differ from the application's version, modules or build options. Logged placeholders are planned with NULL values, so value-dependent access paths may differ.

EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN records access paths, not estimated or measured rows, costs or timing. Query durations and errors require a supported application log; request traces need request identifiers in that telemetry.
A WAL file can retain allocated space after checkpointing. Its size or growth alone does not establish checkpoint starvation or identify a reader holding a snapshot.

deadlocks.message: SQLite records no deadlocks: one writer at a time holds the file
deadlocks.hint: A transaction that can't get the write lock waits busy_timeout, then gets SQLITE_BUSY in the application: its logs say when.

last_actual_plan.message: SQLite's plans have no actual rows or timings: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows the access path only
last_actual_plan.hint: Use the estimated plan; time the statement in the application to see how long it takes.

measures_runs.message: SQLite's plans have no actual rows or timings: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows the access path only
measures_runs.hint: Use the estimated plan; time the statement in the application to see how long it takes.

operator_progress.message: SQLite has no server, so no sessions to show
operator_progress.hint: A writer that has to wait gets SQLITE_BUSY in the application: its logs say when.

periods.message: SQLite keeps no statement history to compare two periods of
periods.hint: Add the log your framework writes to the connection, scan before and after the change, and compare the two reports' queries.

plan_estimates.message: SQLite's plans have no actual rows or timings: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows the access path only
plan_estimates.hint: Use the estimated plan; time the statement in the application to see how long it takes.

sessions.message: SQLite has no server, so no sessions to show
sessions.hint: A writer that has to wait gets SQLITE_BUSY in the application: its logs say when.

sign_in.message: A SQLite file takes no sign-in: Culprit opens it read-only from disk

wait_sample.message: SQLite has no server, so nothing records what it waits on
wait_sample.hint: Time spent waiting for the write lock shows up in the application as SQLITE_BUSY or slow commits.

writes.message: Culprit opens SQLite files read-only, so it never changes one
writes.hint: Run it with the sqlite3 shell or from the application, then scan again to see the effect.
